content:
I would like to start the development of the theory of e-values in Statlib. With @Gaëtan Serré, we wrote a small library of facts about them at https://github.com/RemyDegenne/e-values, which we would like to migrate to Statlib. Gaëtan presented it at the SAVI conference yesterday. The repository contains the following:

  • A definition of an integral for EReal-valued functions. I'm PRing that to Mathlib in #41239 but in the interest of speed I could also PR it to Statlib in parallel.
  • A definition of an e-variable, and a related notion of a randomized e-variable which proved useful
  • A definition of the numeraire e-variable, with a partial proof of its existence following https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18810 (in progress)
  • facts about e-variables and their utilities with an information-theoretic flavor, notably data-processing inequalities
  • e-variable based analogues of Rényi and Chernoff divergences (between two sets of measures) and testing lower bounds derived from their data-processing inequalities
  • some results about the inf-KL / sup-utility duality

So what I'd like to do is to PR first the EReal integral, then the definition of e-variable, and go from there. The reason the EReal integral needs to go first is that our e-variable definition looks a bit unusual:

structure IsEVar (X : 𝓧 → ℝ≥0∞) (S : Set (Measure 𝓧)) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable X := by fun_prop
  eintegral_ne_bot : ∀ μ ∈ S, ∫ᵉ ω, X ω - 1 ∂μ ≠ ⊥
  eintegral_nonpos : ∀ μ ∈ S, ∫ᵉ ω, X ω - 1 ∂μ ≤ 0

So instead of using ∫⁻ ω, X ω ∂μ ≤ 1 (which was our first definition), we write that X-1 has non-positive integral (as an EReal-valued function). The main reason is that it's the right way to extend the definition to measures that are not probability measures and keep most proofs working. We also impose that the integral is not ⊥ (which could happen if the measure is not even finite) because otherwise it becomes too badly behaved.

A practical question about that first PR, which is material that should go to Mathlib: should I create a ForMathlib folder and put everything in there? I'm not sure about the intended folder organization in Statlib.
In LeanMachineLearning I put material intended to be upstreamed to Mathlib/Folder/SubFolder/File.lean into a similar path ForMathlib/Folder/SubFolder/File.lean. Should I do the same here?
Yes! We hope to maintain a ForMathlib folder, also for evalue related stuff, would it be helpful if we also open a project dashboard for evalue related discussion and management?

This zulip topic should be enough for coordination for now I think. If at some point there are many people contributing to e-values in Statlib we could open a project dashboard and all that, but if it's only 2 or 3 people there is no need.
